issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect a StockIngredient constructor with three parameters StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the template provides only a four-parameter constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean). This mismatch will prevent students from using the three-arg constructor as shown in the Main example and as assumed by the exercise instructions and solution, causing compilation errors or confusion about which constructor to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template StockIngredient class provide the three-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int) (either by adding an overloaded constructor delegating to the existing one or by replacing the four-arg constructor), so it matches the problem statement, the example Main usage, and the solution. Alternatively, update the problem statement and solution to explicitly require the four-argument constructor (and adjust examples) if the boolean parameter is intentional.

issues.description: The StockIngredient constructor is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement's class diagram and the solution implementation use a 3-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int), while the template defines a 4-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean strictValidation). This mismatch (including the extra parameter name strictValidation) breaks the conceptual/API mapping: example usage in Main and the exercise description expect the 3-arg constructor and will not compile against the template. Students will be confused about which constructor to use and may waste time resolving this unintended discrepancy.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template API with the problem statement and solution by providing a 3-argument constructor in the template. For example, add a constructor: public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) { this(name, price, quantity, false); } or change the existing constructor to the 3-arg signature so that Main and the exercise description match the template.
